findings: The first plan brings together epidemiology, physiology, disease mechanisms, prevention and health psychology. Methods, sociology, law and communication supply a population and policy context. Experimental Methods follows Social Psychology and the statistics gateway.

The second addresses exposure, climate, healthy environments and governance. Epidemiology stays in term one alongside the regional team research course. Introductory Brain & Behavior and Medical & Health Psychology replace general leadership and Earth’s Resources to retain an explicit health strand. Environmental and energy courses provide context for risks and interventions and do not by themselves teach clinical care or health-system management.
Both internal plans meet current offering and prerequisite rules. No reader-facing UCR programme is selected before the external evidence is complete.
